title: sse plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `sse` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component SseConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

SseConfig.description: Plugin: sse — Server-Sent Events stream handler. Validates SSE client criteria, shapes requests, and ensures proper streaming response headers. Unknown keys and non-object configs are rejected. Explicit null members are rejected; omitted keys keep defaults. wrap_non_sse_responses implies client-visible text/event-stream for wrapped responses.

require_get_method.description: Reject non-GET requests with 405 (SSE is read-only). While this or require_accept_header is enabled, the checks are route admission policy: a native gRPC or WebSocket request to the route, which runs only plain-HTTP plugins, is refused with 403 (rejection phase route_protocol_admission) instead of skipping them.

require_accept_header.description: Require an affirmative Accept: text/event-stream entry (406 otherwise; q=0, malformed, or duplicate quality is not affirmative). While this or require_get_method is enabled, native gRPC and WebSocket requests to the route are refused with 403 (rejection phase route_protocol_admission).

strip_accept_encoding.description: Strip Accept-Encoding to prevent compressed responses breaking SSE framing

add_no_buffering_header.description: Add X-Accel-Buffering: no to disable nginx/ALB response buffering

strip_content_length.description: Remove Content-Length from SSE responses (streams are indefinite)

retry_ms.description: EventSource reconnection hint in milliseconds, prepended as a retry: field when wrapping, and written once ahead of the first bytes of a streamed genuine backend text/event-stream 2xx response (as its own line, so it dispatches no event; a later backend retry: field overrides it). Never written into a stream under a non-identity Content-Encoding, a Cache-Control: no-transform stream, or a 206/226 response. Admitted over the JSON numeric VALUE, so an exact integer-valued number (2500.0) is accepted exactly as 2500 is; fractional values and magnitudes outside the unsigned 64-bit range above are rejected.

force_sse_content_type.description: Force Content-Type: text/event-stream even if backend returns something else. Not applied to a response carrying Cache-Control: no-transform (RFC 9110 section 7.7 forbids an intermediary changing Content-Type on one), to 206/226 responses, or to bodies under a non-identity Content-Encoding, whether or not wrap_non_sse_responses is enabled.

wrap_non_sse_responses.description: Wrap non-SSE response bodies in data: ...\n\n SSE event framing (enables response buffering). Implies client-visible text/event-stream for wrapped responses and composes with force_sse_content_type. Wrapping and its relabel are declined together — the origin representation is forwarded unchanged — for 206/226 responses, responses carrying Cache-Control: no-transform (RFC 9110 section 7.7, which also blocks force_sse_content_type), and bodies under a non-identity Content-Encoding. A framed event that exceeds the effective response-body ceiling returns the gateway capacity refusal instead of the unframed body. Only responses this plugin's after_proxy relabelled are framed, so synthetic responses (response_mock, terminate-mode serverless_function, cache hits) keep their own body and media type.
